minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 26, 2016

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Ury at 5:05 p.m., on April 26, 2016, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 21, 2016, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum (arrived at 5:30 p.m.)
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS

At the hour of 5:05 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m.
with all five City Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Mayor Ury

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

City Council Minutes  1  April 26, 2016
 PRESENTATIONS

P1. Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Ury presented a certificate of commendation to "Marine of the Quarter" Lance
  Corporal Cody L. Cunningham. "Noncommissioned Officer of the Quarter" Sergeant Jordan
  M. Davis was unable to attend the meeting.

P2. Arts Alive Presentation

  The City Council received the presentation from Dru Maurer and several artists who will be
  creating chalk art or selling artwork at Arts Alive on April 30 and May 1, 2016.

P3. Waste Management and EcoNomics presentation on AB 1826 (Mandatory Commercial
  Organics Recycling)

  The City Council received the presentation from Trevor Blythe from EcoNomics, Inc. and
  Tom Koutroulis from Waste Management.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

John Bouldin, M.V.: stated that crime in his neighborhood has gone up quite a bit and he shared
some statistics.

Don Croucher, M.V.: supported what Mr. Bouldin said and he expressed his own concerns about
break-ins in their neighborhood.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 6, and 9 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.
City Council Minutes  2  April 26, 2016
 2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of April 12, 2016, as presented.

4.  Check Register Dated April 8, 2016 in the Amount of $446,335.98

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  2015 Residential Resurfacing-Slurry Seal (CIP 838)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful
  performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with
  the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

7.  Water Conservation Rebates Awarded

  (1) Adopted Resolution 16-14 Amending the FY 2015/16 Budget to Recognize $56,113.42
  in Water Conservation Rebates and Appropriate Funds for ongoing Water Conservation
  Efforts; (2) approved Second Amendment to the existing contract with W.M. Vandergeest
  Landscape Care Inc. for (Area 2) and issue a change order in an amount not to exceed
  $15,000.

8.  Beverage Container Recycling Program

  Adopted Resolution 16-15 Authorizing Submittal of Application for Payment Programs and
  Related Authorizations.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Check Register Dated April 1, 2016 in the Amount of $3,411,028.31

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about a payment made to the County of Ventura for
  Gartner Core Research renewal.

  Director of Information Technology Jackie Alexander responded that Gartner is a research
  firm that is used statewide to provide information on technology trends. The City of Mission
  Viejo participates in a contract that was negotiated by the County of Ventura. The
  information is not available for public use but it helps the IT Department to manage its
  business processes and to stay on top of industry trends.

City Council Minutes  3  April 26, 2016
   Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

6.  Claims Against the City - Elaheh Mafi

  Council Member Schlicht asked the City Attorney track the lawsuit and Supreme Court
  ruling about fallen trees causing injury.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Ury, to reject the claim.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

9.  Purchase of Building Access Control System

  Council Member Schlicht inquired, on behalf of a resident, about the protocols for lost or
  revoked cards and how tightly the cards are controlled. She recommended a 6-month check
  to see that old users are purged and that all panic buttons work after software updates.

  Director of Information Technology Jackie Alexander answered the questions and outlined
  the City’s current and projected controls with the new building access system.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to
  approve entering into agreement and issuance of purchase order to RD Systems, Inc. in the
  amount of $114,562.80 for purchase and implementation of a Lenel Building Access Control
  System plus a 10% contingency for a total project amount of $126,019.08.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

10. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report
City Council Minutes  4  April 26, 2016
   Council Member Sachs presented the report.

11. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

12. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Mayor Ury presented the report.

13. PACE Program Ad Hoc Committee - PACE Information Packet for Residents

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to
  approve the information packet for resident education regarding PACE programs with the
  use of Alternate A for the cover letter.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

STAFF REPORTS

14. Report of Financial Controls

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  By consensus, the City Council directed that an audit team is hired to set up criteria and a
  timeline for conducting an entity-wide risk assessment and internal audit of one or two City
  departments per year. The Council also discussed the formation of an Ad Hoc Committee
  comprised of two Council Members and the City Manager to locate the auditing firm and to
  determine the scope of the project.

  Staff agreed to return at the next City Council meeting with a report outlining options for the
  proposed audit.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Council Member Raths

16. Report on Financial Controls; Direct further review

  Council Member Raths presented his report. Action on this matter was taken with agenda
  item 14.

City Council Minutes  5  April 26, 2016
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

15. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs announced that he had nothing to report.

Council Member Schlicht

17. Term Limits with Lifetime Ban

  Council Member Schlicht presented her agenda report.

  Shelly Blair, M.V.: expressed her support for City Council Member term limits with a lifetime
  ban.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Raths, to push this
  matter forward for the November 2016 ballot.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Schlicht
  NOES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  ABSENT:  None

Council Member Schlicht discussed the upcoming Sheriff’s Department contract renewal. She
stated that crime is going up and it is still her position that the City should go back down to 6
motorcycles and add 5 additional squad cars. She said that according to the Orange County
Register newspaper, Mission Viejo had a 20-25% uptick in crime along with the cities of Lake
Forest, Aliso Viejo and Dana Point. Council Member Schlicht noted that 30% of the City’s budget
goes towards public safety and she believes that tax dollars would be better spent on police cruisers
versus motorcycles. She said that cars are more visible and therefore help to deter crime and they
are safer for the officers. Council Member Schlicht stated that she was disappointed with the 4-1
vote for Council Member term limits with a lifetime ban and she doesn't know why her colleagues
are fearful about allowing voters to decide. She discussed the PACE program and said that it can
be expensive when a resident tries to sell their house and buyers do not want to assume the debt,
nor do banks. In closing, she read the following quote: "Honesty means never having to look over
your shoulder."

City Council Minutes  6  April 26, 2016
 Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum congratulated La Paz Elementary School on a great International
Fair. She outlined her attendance at recent events including the Orange County Sheriff’s
Department Medal of Valor luncheon where two Mission Viejo residents received awards for
risking their lives to save others and the City’s Arbor Day/Earth Day volunteer planting event.
Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum encouraged residents to attend the upcoming Arts Alive festival and the
Swim Meet of Champions at the Marguerite Aquatics Center. Referring to comments made earlier
in the evening about public safety, Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum said that Neighborhood Watch is a
great program and safety is very important to her. She plans to host a town hall meeting on the
topic in the near future and she encouraged residents to be on the lookout for that.

Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury stated that the City’s decision on the Advanced Water Purification plant is getting
noticed. He has been asked to speak tomorrow at the Orange County Business Council’s economic
development committee meeting where he will discuss the water project and economic
development in Mission Viejo.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:15 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, May 10, 2016, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of May 10, 2016

City Council Minutes  7  April 26, 2016
